authority: One source-built Core with PostgreSQL shared by two replicas; no adapter refresh store.
states: Current refresh verifier lives in Core/PostgreSQL.
Refreshing the current credential mints candidate child tokens in the same session without retiring the current verifier.
A child's stateful access verification or child refresh atomically promotes its verifier. Other candidates cannot extend independent refresh chains after that promotion.
Before promotion, loss of the candidate response permits retry of the current credential without a time-based grace period.
After promotion, a stale parent or sibling refresh produces TOKEN_THEFT_DETECTED. The default Node SDK handler then revokes the session through Core.
After committed revocation, refresh and online verification fail. Unrelated sessions remain usable. Offline JWT residual validity is a separate profile.
client_constraints_under_test: The maintained React/Session fetch interceptor coordinates cookie refreshes in a shared browser context.
A raw header client concurrently using both candidate branches is not qualified; selected-child loss caused by theft handling must remain a failed availability observation.
fault_points: Drop request before proxy forwards to Core; this is not a failure inside a database transaction.
Consume complete real Core refresh response then drop before delivery to SDK.
Deliver only the first eight response-body bytes to SDK then close transport.
Lose the committed child-promotion response; confirm stale parent on the other replica, SIGKILL and restart only temporary Core B, then check persisted policy.
still_required: Transaction-internal pre-commit failures, database crash/failover and broader ordering/security acceptance.
SDK crash or failed revocation after Core theft response; Core legacy theft response alone does not revoke.
Other SDKs, cookie/header policies, browsers, native hardware and full original profile matrix.
Independent security review and final engine selection; identity and licensing blockers remain unchanged.
All original CDI5.3 contract entries and separately characterized CDI5.6 failures remain preserved.
